historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (25.8-38.5%) is a large positive outlier vs revenue/FCF CAGRs and is NOT used as the growth proxy: Autodesk ran negative/near-zero shareholders' equity from FY2017-FY2020 (aggressive buybacks exceeding retained earnings), so the equity base-year denominator is depressed and the resulting 'CAGR' overstates true compounding -- it is a capital-structure artifact, not a growth signal. Revenue 3yr CAGR (12.9%) is used as the anchor instead, corroborated by owner-FCF 5yr CAGR of 11.0% and the FY2027 guided growth of ~15.5%. EPS 5yr CAGR is negative only because FY2021 EPS ($5.44) included a one-off tax benefit spike (net income $1,208M on $3,790M revenue, a 31.9% net margin vs. ~15-18% in adjacent years) -- not a growth signal either; EPS 3yr CAGR (11.4%) off a cleaner base is consistent with revenue growth.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 guided growth (~15.5%) decelerating to 6% terminal as the installed base matures; EBITDA margin climbs from 25.5% to a 30% steady state as the new transaction/agency model's margin-optimization phase completes per CFO guidance; SBC load fades from ~15% toward ~9% of revenue as the business scales.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI-driven cross-sell, sustained 20%+ construction growth, and successful MaintainX integration extend the 'Design, Make, Operate' platform; margin overshoots to 33% as S&M efficiency gains compound; requires several independent execution wins.
scenario_narratives.bear: Macro softness in Europe/APAC and intensifying competition from Dassault/Siemens/PTC (manufacturing) and Procore/Trimble (construction) compress growth to mid-single digits; MaintainX integration proves costly and margin optimization stalls near 23-25%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Autodesk is a high-quality, ~97%-recurring-revenue SaaS platform with a dominant, hard-to-displace position in AEC/BIM (AutoCAD, Revit, the DWG file-format standard) and a leading-but-more-contested position in manufacturing/PLM. The investment case rests on continued margin expansion as the multi-year transaction-model transition (agency/commission model, annual billing for multi-year contracts) completes, layered onto secular digitization tailwinds (cloud platforms, AI-assisted design) and the new MaintainX-enabled expansion into building/asset operations. The owner-FCF DCF (component build, 10-year horizon since FY2026 owner-FCF margin of 18.5% is still well below its projected mature level) values the business on cash actually available to shareholders after fully charging stock-based compensation -- the single largest swing factor in this model given SBC+equity-award-taxes run ~15% of revenue.
key_risks_to_valuation: MaintainX integration risk -- the largest acquisition in company history, funded from cash reserves, could distract management and delay the margin-optimization narrative the base case depends on

SBC assumed to decline from ~15% to ~9% of revenue over 10 years; if competitive retention pressure (Dassault, Siemens, PTC, Procore) keeps grant levels elevated, both house and street intrinsic values are overstated

Cyclical AEC/manufacturing capex exposure -- a macro slowdown (flagged specifically for Europe/APAC) would compress new-seat growth and EBA renewals below the FY2027 guidance anchor this model's Year-1 growth rate rests on

The 'new transaction model' billing shift continues to distort billings/cash-flow comparability into FY2027 per the Analysis JSON, meaning the FY2026 owner-FCF margin used as the anchor may itself still carry some transition noise rather than being a clean steady-state read

Terminal value is 20x-capped (base case) rather than pure Gordon growth, but still represents a meaningful share of enterprise value given the 10-year explicit horizon -- see terminal_pct_of_value per scenario

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 185.50-326.20
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL company-concept API (CIK0000769397) for FY2026 10-K and Q1/Q2 FY2027 10-Q anchors (revenue, cash, debt, diluted shares); research/ADSK/Reports/ADSK_Metrics.csv and ADSK.duckdb core_metrics/kpis tables for the historical FY2016-FY2026 series (revenue, EBITDA, FCF, SBC, equity_award_taxes, buybacks, cash_taxes)
data_sources.qualitative: research/ADSK/Reports/ADSK_Analysis.json (guidance, bull/bear case, recent developments including the MaintainX acquisition and resolved SEC/DOJ investigation)

inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL FY2026 10-K (period ended 2026-01-31): StockBasedComp cash-flow add-back $788M + equity_award_taxes (cash taxes withheld on net-share settlement, financing activities) $289M = $1,077M combined; no single combined non-GAAP reconciliation line found in the XBRL facts pulled, so summed per method section 1(a) fallback
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2026-07-31 (Q2 FY2027 10-Q), adjusted pro-forma for the MaintainX acquisition (closed 2026-08-03, ~$1.6B cash consideration) since the valuation date post-dates the close: cash $4,098M actual less $1,600M deal cash = $2,498M pro-forma; debt held flat at $2,500M (deal funded from cash + restricted stock, no new borrowing per company disclosure). Net debt therefore ~$2M (effectively nil) rather than the $1,598M net-cash position shown on the pre-close 10-Q balance sheet.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-07-31 (Q2 FY2027 10-Q weighted-average diluted share count, per SEC XBRL WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding)
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.0% for a large-cap, low-leverage US software company: ~4.1% risk-free (10Y UST), ~5.5% ERP, beta ~1.05-1.1 reflecting moderate cyclicality in AEC/manufacturing capex exposure and elevated near-term integration/leverage risk from the MaintainX deal. No material lease or NCI adjustment needed.
inputs.lease_treatment: not material - Autodesk's operating leases are small (office space); no separate lease line modelled, consistent with a pure SaaS/software cost structure with capex <1% of revenue
inputs.nci_treatment: none - wholly owned, no minority interests
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF (component build), routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md as a SaaS/software operating company (fresh build, no prior DCF or Drivers file existed for ADSK). Fiscal year ends Jan 31; 'FY2026' = year ended 2026-01-31 (the latest completed FY) throughout this file, matching SEC XBRL fy/fp tags -- NOTE the ticker's Metrics.csv/DB period labels for the two most recent quarters ('Q2 2026' $1,934M and 'Q3 2026' $2,046M) are mislabeled and actually correspond to Q1 FY2027 (Feb-Apr 2026) and Q2 FY2027 (May-Jul 2026) per SEC XBRL fy=2027 fp=Q1/Q2 tags -- flagging for a future CSV/DB relabel; this valuation bypasses the mislabeled rows and uses SEC XBRL directly for anchors. Historical owner-FCF margin is volatile (7.1% FY2024 trough to 24.3% FY2023 peak) driven by the multi-year 'new transaction model' billing/agency-model transition (completed through FY2026-27 per Analysis.json); FY2026 owner-FCF margin of 18.5% and management's FY2027 FCF guidance ($2.725-2.75B reported, implying continued owner-FCF margin recovery) are used as the anchor for Year-1, not the FY2024 trough. Interest income not separately disclosed in recent filings (likely netted in other income) and immaterial given near-zero net debt post-MaintainX; not stripped. Share count held FLAT (211M) because SBC is fully expensed in the flows -- buybacks ($1,402M in FY2026, a consistent multi-year repurchase program) are the cash mechanism funding that flat count, already captured in the SBC deduction. MaintainX ($3.6B all-cash acquisition, closed 2026-08-03) is treated as already reflected in the pro-forma balance sheet anchor (net debt ~$0) and its ~$60M H2 FY2027 revenue/~$70M billings contribution is embedded in the FY2027 guidance-based Year-1 growth rate; no separate segment DCF was built for MaintainX given its small initial revenue contribution (~0.7% of guided FY2027 revenue) -- this likely modestly understates MaintainX's medium-term standalone growth contribution to the 'Operate' pillar, a limitation noted for future updates as MaintainX-specific disclosure emerges.

bear.narrative: Bear case: European/APAC macro softness and AEC/manufacturing capex cyclicality (both flagged as risks in the Analysis JSON) compress new-seat growth and EBA renewals well below guidance; Dassault/Siemens/PTC erode share in the less-entrenched manufacturing/PLM segment while Procore/Trimble contest construction tech, capping construction growth well below the current 20%+ pace. MaintainX integration proves costly and distracting (largest deal in company history, funded from cash reserves that would otherwise support buybacks), delaying rather than accelerating the margin-optimization narrative -- EBITDA margin stalls near 23-25% instead of reaching 30%. SBC load declines only slowly as competitive pressure requires continued heavy retention grants. Weighted at 20% given the accounting-investigation overhang is fully resolved (a real de-risking event) but genuine cyclical and competitive risks remain live.

base.narrative: Base case: FY2027 growth tracks management's raised guidance (~15.5%, includes ~$60M H2 MaintainX contribution), then decelerates as the AEC/manufacturing installed base matures and price-increase headroom narrows, settling near 6% terminal growth (secular software/digitization tailwind, GDP-plus). EBITDA margin continues the multi-year climb toward 'best-in-industry' levels the CFO has guided to (25.5% FY2026 actual to 30% steady-state) as the new transaction/agency model completes its margin-optimization phase. SBC+equity-award-tax load declines gradually from ~14.9% of revenue toward ~9% as grant dilution is diluted by a larger revenue base, consistent with a maturing, cash-generative SaaS platform. Cash tax rate ramps from its recent trough (16.3% FY2026, likely stock-comp-deduction-depressed) toward a ~23% normalized blended global rate.

bull.narrative: Bull case: AI-enabled features (Autodesk AI in Fusion/Forma/AutoCAD) and cloud platform migration (Construction Cloud, Fusion) drive accelerated seat expansion and cross-sell beyond the FY2027 guide, construction segment sustains 20%+ growth for longer, and MaintainX integration succeeds faster than expected, extending the 'Design, Make, Operate' platform into a durable new growth vector. Margin optimization from the completed transaction-model transition overshoots the 'best-in-industry' target as S&M efficiency gains compound with operating leverage, pushing EBITDA margin to 33% steady state. Requires several independent things to go right (AI monetization, MaintainX integration, sustained construction growth, no competitive share loss to Procore/Dassault) -- kept at 35% weight given the multi-legged nature of the case.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default shifted slightly from 15/50/35 toward bear (20%) given the elevated near-term integration/execution load from the largest acquisition in company history (MaintainX, $3.6B) layered onto an already-complex multi-year transaction-model transition, and genuine cyclical exposure to AEC/manufacturing capex specifically flagged as a risk. Bull trimmed to 30% because it requires several independent things to go right (AI monetization, MaintainX integration, sustained 20%+ construction growth, no share loss) rather than a single catalyst. The SEC/DOJ accounting-investigation overhang is fully resolved without restatement (a genuine de-risking event, both closed by August 2025), which is why bear is not weighted higher still.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
